KROWNLANDIA COMMUNITY LIBRARY · NOVEMBER 5, 2026

Krownlandia: Open source resources

A guide to the public code, documentation and contribution work that supports the Krownlandia prototype.

Current status: the public source snapshot covers hosted version 252, including Riverbend practice pottery and the repeatable release-check command. GitHub and Sites do not automatically synchronize; later changes require a reviewed refresh.

Verified GitHub progress

github.com/lisachandler/krownlandia was refreshed on November 5, 2026 from hosted version 252. See the public commit history for the exact revision. The previous snapshot was version 233, dated October 29.

The refresh includes recent photo/video recovery, Library and Eldergrove guidance, the optional Riverbend pottery workshop, visitor reports and selected release checks. Private publication records, account identifiers, credentials and registered hosting configuration are excluded. The administrator log uses an empty public fixture. Browser rendering, codecs and assistive-technology checks remain unverified.

Trying the public snapshot

The repository README documents serving the static game with Python 3: python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory dist, then opening http://localhost:8000 in a WebGL-capable browser. It also documents npm ci and npm run dev. These commands are reported from the README, not newly executed for this document.

Browser progress is local to its host. A local copy does not automatically share saves with the hosted Gateway. Preserve exports before trying another host. Example documented checks are node tests/community-walk.mjs, node tests/backup.mjs and node tests/journal.mjs.

License and attribution status

The README says no project-wide open-source license has been selected. This document retains Lisa's requested title, but does not describe all Krownlandia material as licensed open source. Three.js has its own retained license at dist/vendor/LICENSE. Community text, branding, generated artwork, linked sticker artwork and other assets require their own attribution and permission review before a broader reuse policy is announced.

Proposed next contributions

  1. Prepare a reviewed, sanitized GitHub refresh from the current Site source; exclude private hosting records, credentials and administrator configuration.
  2. Record the matching hosted version and commit in each public release. Document which direction synchronization occurs and who reviews it.
  3. Choose a project license with the relevant rights holders; inventory asset permissions and keep original community credits.
  4. Add contribution guidance, reproducible bug reports and a clear test checklist. Avoid publishing visitor emails or private progress in issues.
  5. Track multiplayer, server rewards and Unity milestones as explicitly proposed work, with completion checks and separate reviews.
